subject: POC trial environment: hosted vs dedicated sandbox vs VPC - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sana Khan <sana.khan@acmeai.com>, Ethan Rivera <ethan.rivera@acmeai.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC trial environment: hosted vs dedicated sandbox vs VPC - recap & next steps

Thanks for a productive call this morning — summary and proposed next steps below.

High-level objective
- Run a 3-week POC to validate latency, cost, and integration points for Acme AI's "Answers" feature using a 3rd-party knowledge base.

Success criteria (what we agreed)
1) 95th percentile tail latency < 250ms on sample QPS (see table attached)
2) Token-level cost estimate within 20% of forecasted budget
3) No PII persisted in logs; audit logging available for review
4) Seamless integration with your auth flow and doc ingestion pipeline

Evaluation plan & ownership
- Redwood (Marissa): provide POC template, baseline test harness, and two environment options (hosted trial, dedicated sandbox).
- Redwood (Dev): deliver network requirements and quick-start scripts; run one joint smoke test.
- Acme (Sana / Ethan): provide sample dataset, internal security contact, and target QPS for sim tests.

Environment options (tradeoffs we discussed)
- Hosted trial: fastest to start (API keys + sample dataset). Good for early validation and perf baselines. Minimal network setup.
- Dedicated sandbox (reserved dev cluster): predictable throughput and isolated capacity for more representative perf testing. Moderate lead time to provision.
- VPC/private trial: strongest data control (customer-managed networking, KMS options). Longer lead time (network + firewall + routing) and security review required.

Attachments: POC_scope_v1.pdf (scope & test plan)

Proposed timeline
- Decision on environment by EOD Fri, Aug 7
- Kickoff + access handed off Mon, Aug 10
- 3-week POC Aug 11 - Aug 30 (target)

Immediate asks
- Sana: confirm preferred environment (hosted | dedicated | VPC) and provide the security contact for the VPC path if needed.
- Ethan: share a representative sample of the dataset and target QPS numbers.

If you confirm hosted, we can have API keys and a baseline in <48 hours. For dedicated or VPC, Dev will outline provisioning steps and ETA.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick follow-up if useful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
-- Attachment: POC_scope_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Sana Khan <sana.khan@acmeai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ethan Rivera <ethan.rivera@acmeai.com>
Cc: Acme AI Security Team <security@acmeai.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC trial environment: hosted vs dedicated sandbox vs VPC - recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers from our side: 

1) Preference: Hosted trial to start (we want to move fast and validate end-to-end). If results look good, iterate to dedicated sandbox for scale tests.
2) Success criteria: agree with your list. Add: model output consistency with our current baseline (we'll provide eval prompts).
3) Security: we need to confirm that logs can be redacted and that we can opt-out of storing session text beyond the POC window. Our security team (cc'd) will want to review the SOC 2 summary and options for audit logs.

Ethan will drop a 1GB sample dataset (anonymized) and target QPS: 15 sustained, 50 spike for short bursts.

Decision next steps: we'll confirm hosted path by end of day Friday (Aug 7).

Best,
Sana Khan
Head of Product, Acme AI
Sana.Khan@acmeai.com

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Sana Khan <sana.khan@acmeai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC trial environment: hosted vs dedicated sandbox vs VPC - technical notes

Thanks — wanted to add a few technical clarifications to help your team choose.

1) Hosted trial (recommended to start):
- Provisioning: we can issue API keys and a sandbox project in <48 hours.
- Data handling: by default, request/response logs are stored for 30 days; we can set a PII redaction policy and enable "no-persist" for the POC on request.
- Limits: we can provision token-rate-limits to match your target QPS.

2) Dedicated sandbox:
- Provides reserved GPU capacity and isolated KV cache to better simulate production.
- Provisioning ETA: ~5 business days depending on cluster sizing.
- Useful if you want to validate sustained 15 QPS with consistent tail-latency under load.

3) VPC/private trial:
- Requires network peering, firewall rules, and optional customer-side routing to our private endpoints.
- Security artifacts needed: an IP allowlist, TLS mutual auth setup (optional), and KMS key ID if you want BYOK.
- Provisioning ETA: 10+ business days (includes security review).

Attachments: redwood_network_diagram.png (shows VPC flow and required firewall rules).

If you confirm hosted, I can run a smoke test with your dataset as soon as Ethan drops it in the shared Drive link. I'll also share a short checklist for the security team to speed the VPC review if you want to explore that down the line.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev@redwood.com
